connection and request limits
for clients: Set limits on the number of connections and requests from clients, preventing resource exhaustion and ensuring fair usage of server resources.
Block bots
with
challenge-based verification
: Keep malicious bots at bay by challenging them to solve puzzles such as cookies, JavaScript tests, captchas, hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA, or Turnstile, effectively blocking unauthorized access.
Block known bad IPs
with external blacklists and DNSBL: Utilize external blacklists and DNS-based blackhole lists (DNSBL) to proactively block known malicious IP addresses, bolstering your defense against potential threats.
And much more...
: BunkerWeb is packed with a plethora of additional security features that go beyond this list, providing you with comprehensive protection and peace of mind.
To delve deeper into the core security features, we invite you to explore the

user interface

Technical support to assist you with configuration

data.title: Rust and WASM for Form Validation
data.author: slau
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了使用Rust和WebAssembly（WASM）进行表单验证的简化方法。过去，使用Rust生成WASM需要复杂的工具链，如Node和Webpack，但现在过程变得更加简化。作者演示了如何创建一个包含Rust web服务器和WASM组件的项目，其中WASM组件用于表单验证。

项目结构包括一个服务器目录和一个WASM目录。首先，需要安装WASM目标并配置`wasm-pack`。然后，通过编辑`Cargo.toml`文件添加必要的依赖和库类型。使用`wasm-pack build --target web`命令生成WASM库。

服务器端使用Rocket框架来处理请求，并渲染包含表单的HTML模板。通过Rust函数验证表单提交的密码是否正确，并返回相应的模板。

整个过程展示了如何在无需复杂前端知识的情况下，利用Rust和WASM实现后端风格的Web开发。这种方法允许在前后端共享相同的代码和数据结构。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust与WebAssembly（WASM）在Web开发中的应用及其优劣

不同观点：
• **zoechi**：认为Dioxus 0.7提供的组件简化了与JavaScript的交互，前景看好，但指出WASM模块的模块化和懒加载是当前的不足，以减少初始下载大小。

• **wasmperson**：
  - 对代码中大量使用`unwrap`表示担忧，认为在某些情况下程序崩溃是不可避免的。
  - 提出WebAssembly最佳实践应包括：主要使用JavaScript处理DOM和Web API，WASM二进制文件应具有窄接口和少量函数，避免依赖第三方包或标准库，并广泛使用可变的“全局”变量。
  - 认为Rust与wasm-bindgen、web-sys的组合策略与上述最佳实践相悖，除非目标是完全避免编写JavaScript。

• **neoneye2**：分享了自己使用Rust代码同时处理前端和后端的经验，并提供了项目示例和实现链接，展示Rust在全栈开发中的实际应用。

• **reactordev**：强烈反对使用WASM处理诸如表单验证等简单任务，认为这是“用炸弹杀苍蝇”，主张WASM应仅用于IPC、Canvas、WebGPU等复杂任务，而非简单的DOM操作。

• **jedisct1**：简短地指出学习JavaScript是更好的选择。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：使用Rust和WebAssembly进行Web开发的合理性与实用性，特别是在处理DOM交互和简单任务时的效率和必要性。
- **技术实现**：讨论了Rust与WebAssembly结合时的技术细节，如错误处理、模块化以及如何有效利用全局变量。
- **实际应用**：展示了全栈Rust项目实例，提供了对Rust和WebAssembly结合使用的实际效果的参考。

总体来看，讨论围绕着Rust与WebAssembly在Web开发中的应用价值、技术实现细节以及与JavaScript的角色分工展开。

Rust and WASM for form validation
Sebastian Lauwers
24th Apr 2025
•
10 min read
•
Tags:
rust
,
wasm
,
programming
,
tech
For a very long time, the Rust WASM story wasn't entirely clear to me. In order to use WASM from Rust you had to use Node, Webpack, and all that jazz. This always turned me off using WebAssembly because it felt too heavy of a toolchain to get going. These days, things are much, much better.
In recent years, Rust and WebAssembly have become much more usable for pure backend-style engineers. When I say “pure backend-style”, I mean people who never wrapped their heads around React, SPAs, and all that stuff. This, unsurprisingly, includes me.
For a very long time, in order to use WASM you were strongly guided towards using Webpack and a whole array of Node-related tools in order to just get started. These days, luckily, the story has become much more streamlined. In today’s tutorial, we’re going to create a quick project which includes both a web server in Rust which renders HTML templates, and a small WASM component (served by the same web server) that does form validation.
Why?
Well, I want to keep a reference handy about how this can be done. But I also want to hear if I’m doing something wrong or suboptimally.
As to why Rust/WASM instead of standard JS or TS? For one, I like to see how far we’ve come with WASM, and there is something very appealing about having the same code shared across the frontend and the backend, especially if it means potentially having the same data structures when serialising/deserialising data from one end to the other.
I’m using form validation as a placeholder. It shows all the crucial aspects to use WASM instead of JS, like wiring up DOM events to Rust functions, and then reacting to those events.
Stack
This post is being written in early-to-mid 2025. And the stack I currently jive with is as follows:
wasm-bindgen 0.2
wasm-pack 0.13
web-sys 0.3
rocket 0.5
I’m not going to do any database-related things or anything, which allows us to keep the dependencies pretty short and sweet. Most of these are library dependencies, however
wasm-pack
is a binary that actually modifies files and prepares them for distribution. This needs to be installed locally:
#
binstall can also be used here
cargo
install wasm-pack
Project structure
Let’s create a directory structure that allows this whole setup to work. One typical approach for this is to have separate crates for the server part, and the actual wasm component. Something like this:
tutorial
├── server
└── wasm
If you want to create things quickly:
mkdir
tutorial
&&
cd
tutorial
cargo
new
--
lib
wasm
cargo
new server
If you prefer to see the entire repo instead of creating all the files yourself, there is full repository available
here
.
WASM setup
Installing wasm as a target
One thing that you might have to do is to get the compiler support to actually produce wasm binaries. Provided you use
rustup
(and you really ought to be using it), this is as simple as:
rustup
target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
You can check which targets you currently have installed with
rustup target list --installed
.
Configuring the wasm crate
Edit
Cargo.toml
and add the following section. This tells the compiler to produce a dynamic library that has a relatively stable ABI. This is similar to building a library for C/C++ interop.
[
lib
]
crate-type
=
[
"
cdylib
"
]
Let’s also pull in some dependencies while we’re editing that file:
[
dependencies
]
wasm-bindgen
=
"
0.2
"
[
dependencies
.
web-sys
]
version
=
"
0.3
"
features
=
[
"
Document
"
,
"
HtmlFormElement
"
,
"
HtmlInputElement
"
,
"
Window
"
,
"
console
"
,
"
Event
"
,
]
At this point, you should be able to build the library in wasm form using the following command:
wasm-pack
build
--
target
web
This will produce a few files in
pkg/

44463916.article_summary:
本文介绍了使用Rust和WebAssembly（WASM）进行表单验证的简化方法。过去，使用Rust生成WASM需要复杂的工具链，如Node和Webpack，但现在过程变得更加简化。作者演示了如何创建一个包含Rust web服务器和WASM组件的项目，其中WASM组件用于表单验证。

项目结构包括一个服务器目录和一个WASM目录。首先，需要安装WASM目标并配置`wasm-pack`。然后，通过编辑`Cargo.toml`文件添加必要的依赖和库类型。使用`wasm-pack build --target web`命令生成WASM库。

服务器端使用Rocket框架来处理请求，并渲染包含表单的HTML模板。通过Rust函数验证表单提交的密码是否正确，并返回相应的模板。

整个过程展示了如何在无需复杂前端知识的情况下，利用Rust和WASM实现后端风格的Web开发。这种方法允许在前后端共享相同的代码和数据结构。
44463916.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust与WebAssembly（WASM）在Web开发中的应用及其优劣

不同观点：
• **zoechi**：认为Dioxus 0.7提供的组件简化了与JavaScript的交互，前景看好，但指出WASM模块的模块化和懒加载是当前的不足，以减少初始下载大小。

• **wasmperson**：
  - 对代码中大量使用`unwrap`表示担忧，认为在某些情况下程序崩溃是不可避免的。
  - 提出WebAssembly最佳实践应包括：主要使用JavaScript处理DOM和Web API，WASM二进制文件应具有窄接口和少量函数，避免依赖第三方包或标准库，并广泛使用可变的“全局”变量。
  - 认为Rust与wasm-bindgen、web-sys的组合策略与上述最佳实践相悖，除非目标是完全避免编写JavaScript。

• **neoneye2**：分享了自己使用Rust代码同时处理前端和后端的经验，并提供了项目示例和实现链接，展示Rust在全栈开发中的实际应用。

• **reactordev**：强烈反对使用WASM处理诸如表单验证等简单任务，认为这是“用炸弹杀苍蝇”，主张WASM应仅用于IPC、Canvas、WebGPU等复杂任务，而非简单的DOM操作。

• **jedisct1**：简短地指出学习JavaScript是更好的选择。

- **技术实现**：讨论了Rust与WebAssembly结合时的技术细节，如错误处理、模块化以及如何有效利用全局变量。
- **实际应用**：展示了全栈Rust项目实例，提供了对Rust和WebAssembly结合使用的实际效果的参考。

data.title: Everything around LLMs is still magical and wishful thinking
data.author: troupo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）和生成式AI在工作中的实际效用和局限性

不同观点：
• tasty_freeze认为，管理层对10倍生产力提升的期望过高。即使编码速度加快，总体生产力提升只有10-15%。Amdahl's law和非编码工作（如思考和沟通）限制了总体生产力的大幅提升。
• hotpotat分享了自己使用LLM（如Cursor和Claude）的成功经验，认为这些工具极大地提高了他的生产力（至少3倍），并使他能够更专注于架构和管理角色。
• martinald指出，LLM在处理Excel和CRM等数据密集型任务中具有巨大潜力，特别是在服务行业中，能够替代人类进行简单的数据转录和处理工作。
• labrador从退休程序员的角度出发，表示对LLM在关键任务中的可靠性持怀疑态度，但认可LLM在头脑风暴和研究等非编码任务中的价值。
• standardUser认为，许多对LLM的批评可能源于不正确的使用方式，自己每天使用LLM解决问题，成功率高达90%，并认为这些工具在小而实用的场景中非常有效。
• AbrahamParangi反驳了对LLM的过度批评，认为尽管存在 imprecision，过去五年中LLM在翻译、转录和代码生成等领域解决了 previously intractable 的问题。
• surglymop对AGI（通用人工智能）术语的使用感到困惑，认为缺乏明确的定义使得讨论变得模糊，并希望能有更严谨的理论框架来定义AGI。
• kgeist分享了自己公司使用LLM转录客户电话的成功案例，认为LLM在自然语言处理方面非常有用，尽管存在过度炒作，但其实际价值不容忽视。
• djoldman引用了一些知名技术专家的观点，认为GenAI对相当多的人具有显著的帮助，即使具体提升幅度因人而异。
• alganet担心LLM技术的广泛误用和投资浪费问题，认为这种趋势难以逆转，公司已经全力投入。
• jjtheblunt引用Clarke's third law，认为足够先进的技术难以与魔法区分，暗示LLM技术的先进性。
• dcre提到LLM帮助的系统性和研究性问题，反对将LLM的作用简单地贬低为无用。
• cedws指出LLM的两个基本限制：上下文大小和提示注入问题，认为这些限制在实际应用中可能导致严重问题，但常常被忽视。
• ibaikov将LLM与加密货币和NFT的炒作进行对比，认为人们往往只关注新技术的表面 hype，而忽视其复杂性和潜在发展。
• orbital-decay讨论了LLM的非确定性问题，认为现代LLM的非确定性远小于人们想象，且其准确性在需要一致结果的情况下表现良好。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及LLM的实际应用场景，如代码生成、数据转录和自然语言处理等，强调了其在不同领域的不同效用。
• 对LLM的过度炒作和实际效果之间的差距进行了反思，指出需要更理性和系统的评估。
• 讨论了LLM的技术局限性和潜在风险，如提示注入和上下文限制，这些问题在实际应用中可能导致严重后果。
• 对AGI定义的讨论反映了对新兴技术术语和概念的理论需求，以及在技术讨论中严谨定义的重要性。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要列出了几类内容板块。首先是"feature articles"（专题文章），通常是深入探讨特定主题的文章。其次是"codesod"，可能包含与编程或代码相关的内容。接下来是"error'd"，通常涉及错误或故障的讨论和解决方案。然后是"forums"（论坛），指用户交流和讨论的社区板块。此外还有"other articles"（其他文章），涵盖不属于上述分类的其他内容。最后是"random article"（随机文章），用户可以随机浏览不同主题的文章。文章整体为网站内容的导航或介绍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件项目外包中的问题及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• donatj：外包团队没有遵循明确指示，擅自使用新框架并添加了不必要的适配层，导致原项目的维护性变差。这引发了多次返工，最终项目方自己修复了问题并解雇了外包团队。争议焦点在于外包团队没有按照要求进行简单的维护，而是进行了过度修改。
• delifue：该问题反映了没有从根本原因解决问题的常见错误，类似于其他领域（如SQL注入、Windows权限控制、反恶意软件）中通过表面修复带来副作用的情况。强调通过正确的技术手段（如使用预处理语句）解决问题。
• kgeist：认为这种情况很常见，尤其是在处理SQL注入问题上，很多网站依赖第三方安全插件，而不是从根本上解决问题。
• nine_k：引用俄罗斯谚语，指出为了省钱而选择廉价外包最终可能付出更高代价，暗示低成本外包可能导致更高的后续成本。
• userbinator：以幽默方式提到一种常见错误（"clbuttic" bug），进一步强调了外包团队可能犯的低级错误。
• AdieuToLogic：引用xkcd漫画中“Bobby Tables”的例子，以幽默方式呼应SQL注入问题。
• mjcohen：与主帖内容无关，但提到了与“Inception”电影相关的技术讨论，属于完全题外的技术性讨论。

补充讨论：
• 外包项目的失败通常源于沟通不畅和外包团队未按要求执行。
• 讨论中多次提到SQL注入问题及其不当处理方式，强调了从根本上解决技术问题的重要性。
• 幽默和题外话（如“clbuttic”bug和“Inception”讨论）为技术讨论增添了趣味性，但并未深入项目主题。

data.title: Serving 200M requests per day with a CGI-bin
data.author: mustache_kimono
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了使用90年代的CGI技术在现代处理高流量请求的可行性。作者回忆自己1990年代末使用CGI进行网页开发的经历，并指出CGI每次请求都启动和终止进程的方式曾被认为效率低下，因此出现了PHP和FastCGI等技术。然而，随着硬件性能的提升，使用Go和Rust等现代语言可以显著提升CGI效率。实验显示，在AMD 3700X的16线程处理器上，CGI程序每秒可处理2400多个请求，每日可达2亿次。CGI因其独立进程特性，能有效利用多核CPU。作者认为，或许应该重新采用类似1998年的方式开发网页应用，但需结合现代语言如Go和Rust。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CGI技术的优劣以及其在现代开发中的适用性

不同观点：
• **Kragen的观点**：Kragen认为即使使用Python，CGI在当下仍然足够快，尤其是在高流量网站的情况下，CGI的启动时间不会成为瓶颈。然而，他对Python社区移除像CGI这样稳定技术的做法表示不满，并考虑转向JS或Lua。

• **Ivovk的观点**：Ivovk指出，当需要连接外部资源如数据库时，CGI的表现不佳。连接池技术在维持高效连接方面至关重要，因此通常需要一个持续运行的web应用进程。

• **Tractor8626的观点**：Tractor8626质疑CGI在"hello world"应用中2400 rps的表现，认为这种性能不佳，且代码并没有因此变得更简单。

• **Jarofgreen的观点**：Jarofgreen提到Apache的.htaccess功能在性能上的权衡，虽然现代硬件使得性能损失可接受，但在大多数情况下，将配置放在主配置文件中仍是更优选择。

• **Faizshah的观点**：Faizshah认为CGI或FastCGI在快速原型和工作流中仍有价值，尤其是在允许客户通过自定义代码扩展工具时。

• **Petesergeant的观点**：Petesergeant提到mod_php在PHP流行中的重要性，并指出PHP通过mod_php实现了快速运行，而Perl则需要更多的配置和思考。

• **Slashdave的观点**：Slashdave回忆起CGI因安全问题而非性能被淘汰的历史，质疑当前对CGI性能的批评。

• **Aaronblohowiak的观点**：Aaronblohowiak认为fork()在过去30年中变得更便宜，CGI在无需复杂连接的情况下表现良好，但现代需求可能需要像Istio这样的工具。

• **Jekwoooooe的观点**：Jekwoooooe指出，现代技术栈不仅关注性能，还关注开发速度和便利性。

44476716.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Serving 200 million requests per day with a cgi-bin
(
via
) Jake Gold tests how well 90s-era CGI works today, using a Go + SQLite CGI program running on a 16-thread AMD 3700X.
Using CGI on modest hardware, it’s possible to serve 2400+ requests per second or 200M+ requests per day.
I got my start in web development with CGI back in the late 1990s - I was a huge fan of
NewsPro
, which was effectively a weblog system before anyone knew what a weblog was.
CGI works by starting, executing and terminating a process for every incoming request. The nascent web community quickly learned that this was a bad idea, and invented technologies like PHP and
FastCGI
to help avoid that extra overhead and keep code resident in-memory instead.
This lesson ended up baked into my brain, and I spent the next twenty years convinced that you should
never
execute a full process as part of serving a web page.
Of course, computers in those two decades got a
lot
faster. I finally overcame that twenty-year core belief in 2020, when
I built datasette-ripgrep
, a Datasette plugin that shells out to the lightning fast
ripgrep
CLI tool (written in Rust) to execute searches. It worked great!
As was
pointed out on Hacker News
, part of CGI's problem back then was that we were writing web scripts in languages like Perl, Python and Java which had not been designed for lightning fast startup speeds. Using Go and Rust today helps make CGI-style requests a whole lot more effective.
Jake notes that CGI-style request handling is actually a great way to take advantage of multiple CPU cores:
These days, we have servers with 384 CPU threads. Even a small VM can have 16 CPUs. The CPUs and memory are much faster as well.
Most importantly, CGI programs, because they run as separate processes, are excellent at taking advantage of many CPUs!
Maybe we should start coding web applications like it's 1998, albeit with Go and Rust!

data.title: Fast Code Is Easy. Measuring It Is Hard
data.author: auc
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了算法交易系统中延迟的测量和优化挑战。在高频交易中，速度至关重要，工程师们竭尽全力优化代码和网络路径以减少执行时间。然而，测量程序的速度和实际延迟非常复杂，因为需要考虑多个层次的因素，甚至测量本身也会增加程序的开销，影响准确性。

文章通过Python伪代码示例，说明如何测量交易策略的延迟，从计算模型估值到发送订单的各个步骤。初步方法包括在关键函数周围添加计时器，但这种方法存在缺陷，比如未包含发送订单的时间、观测所有市场交易而非仅触发订单的交易等。此外，使用`datetime.now()`作为计时函数本身较慢，可能影响程序性能。改进方法是使用更精确的计时器如`time.perf_counter_ns()`，但仍未涵盖网络I/O等关键路径元素。

最终，文章强调要全面理解交易系统的延迟，必须追踪从网络数据包接收到订单发送的整个过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何正确测量代码性能以及编写快速代码的难度

不同观点：
• weinzierl认为，测量代码性能是编写快速代码的先决条件，且测量非常困难。他指出人们常犯的两个错误：只测量一次和仅采用平均值作为运行时间指标。他建议至少测量三次以了解数据的变异性，并强调最小值比平均值更适合比较代码版本的性能。

• tombert通过自身经历说明了 benchmarking 并发代码的困难，尤其是在使用 async 代码时。他遇到的问题是，由于 .NET 调度器的影响，测试结果不稳定，时间差异很大。这让他意识到 benchmarking 具有欺骗性，并对他之后的性能测试工作产生了深远影响。

• am17an指出，在测量性能时，不仅要测量发送指令的延迟，还要测量决策计算的时间，这两者对系统的吞吐量和延迟都很重要。他还提到使用 L1/L2 交换机的时间戳来测量端到端延迟，可以避免时钟漂移等问题。

• omgtehlion针对高频交易（HFT）的背景提出，测量性能在这种场景下相对简单，可以直接通过网络光纤的进出测量时间，且不会影响生产环境的延迟。

• nine_k认为，编写快速代码本身不难，但要保持代码持续快速则很困难，尤其在不进行测量的情况下。他建议将粗略的性能测试加入 CI/CD 流程中，以快速检测性能回退问题。

• iammabd补充说，大多数人只为“happy path”编写代码，很少有人关注代码在高压条件下的运行表现。

补充讨论：
• 测量中的变异性和数据分布问题被多次提及，尤其是平均值在测量中的局限性。
• 不同应用场景下（如 HFT 和并发代码），测量性能的方法和难度有所不同。
• 创建合适的测试框架和将性能测试集成到开发流程中的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 测量性能的难度和如何正确进行性能测试是讨论的核心争议点，尤其是对并发代码和不同应用场景的测量方法存在不同见解。

How fast is it really? On latency, measurement, and optimization in algorithmic trading systems
byÂ
Brett Harrison
Blog
"The speed of light sucks." - John Carmack
â
Software engineers within the world of low-latency automated trading (colloquially known as "high-frequency trading" or HFT) obsess over speed. From purchasing private bandwidth between microwave towers to analyzing x86 instructions from different compiler versions, those with experience in this industry have seen colossal time and expense committed to the problem of optimizing code and network paths for minimal execution times.
But how does one actually measure how fast a program is? To the uninitiated, it sounds like a simple task. However, there are many layers of complexity in measuring the true latency of a trading system, or even defining what to measure in the first place. Understanding latencies in algorithmic trading systems can present Heisenberg-esque dilemmas, where the more code you write to measure latency the more overhead you add to your program and therefore the more inaccurate your measurements become.
At Architect we have been using a combination techniques to measure the latency of various codepaths and processes that comprise our institutional trading technology suite. Let's explore some solutions to these problems.
--
Let's say you've written an algorithmic trading strategy. Your strategy reacts to market trades in an instrument, perhaps by computing a proprietary model valuation, and sends an order in that instrument provided certain conditions are met. You would like to measure the time that this reaction takes
in a reproducible way
, so that you can reduce the time as much as possible. Let's use Python-style pseudocode to describe the program (although in practice it is most common to use languages like, C, C++, and Rust where optimal program latencies are required):
â
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
A reasonable place to start in understanding the latency of your critical codepath is to wrap timers around the functions doing the heavy lifting:
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
start_time = datetime.now()
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
end_time = datetime.now()
self.add_time_sample(end_time - start_time)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
The function
self.add_time_sample
would add the elapsed time to a histogram that you could print statistics for at the end of your programâs lifecycle, or on some regular basis based on time or number of samples observed.
There are many issues with the above approach:
It measures the time required to compute the order decision, but does not include the time it takes to send the actual order.
It observes computation time on every market trade, rather than just the trades that result in orders â this can bias results because the most interesting times to send orders may be the ones where your program is running the slowest due to volume of market events or other factors.
datetime.now()
itself is a slow, expensive function that can impact the runtime speed and memory profile of the code above, which adds up if your program is already operating on a microsecond-timescale. The typical way to fix this last issue is to use native performance counters that most programming language have primitives to access.
Hereâs a new code sample that attempts to fix the above:
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
start_time = time.perf_counter_ns()
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
end_time = time.perf_counter_ns()
self.add_time_sample(end_time - start_time)
This is an improvement, but are we really getting at the full latency of the trading system? The above doesnât include significant elements of the critical path, including the time to parse the market trade update, or anything involving network I/O. Letâs take a step back and trace a market data update through the complete critical path of the
automated trading system (ATS)
:
Network packet containing the market trade hits the network card of the box where the ATS is running (sent from the exchange)
The packet is passed to the runtime of the ATS
The ATS parses the bytes of the packet to pull out necessary fields (such as trade price or trade size)
The ATS computes a model value and makes a decision to send an order
The internal memory representation of the order is converted to the protocol of the exchange that the order is being sent to
The ATS makes function calls to

Historian Jennifer Cromack points out the word “Slavery” on a recently found, 178-year-old anti-slavery scroll at Grotonwood, the home mission of The American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts, Thursday, June 26, 2025, in Groton, Mass. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)
By
Associated Press
UPDATED:
July 3, 2025 at 11:43 AM EDT
By MICHAEL CASEY
GROTON, Mass. (AP) — Jennifer Cromack was combing through the American Baptist archive when she uncovered a slim box among some 18th and 19th century journals. Opening it, she found a scroll in pristine condition.
A closer look revealed the 5-foot-long (1.5-meter-long) document was a handwritten declaration titled “A Resolution and Protest Against Slavery,” signed by 116 New England ministers in
Boston
and adopted March 2, 1847. Until its discovery in May at the archives in Groton, Massachusetts, American Baptist officials worried the
anti-slavery document
had been lost forever after fruitless searches at Harvard and
Brown universities
and other locations. A copy was last seen in a 1902 history book.
“I was just amazed and excited,” Cromack, a retired teacher who volunteers at the archive, said. “We made a find that really says something to the people of the state and the people in the country. … It speaks of their commitment to keeping people safe and out of situations that they should not be in.”
The document offers a glimpse into an emerging debate over slavery in the 18th century in the Northeast. The document was signed 14 years before the start of the Civil War as a growing number of religious leaders were starting to speak out against slavery.
Historian Jennifer Cromack holds a recently found, 178-year-old anti-slavery scroll at Grotonwood, the home mission of The American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts, Thursday, June 26, 2025, in Groton, Mass. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)
Historian Jennifer Cromack, left, and Rev. Diane Badger unfurl a recently found, 178-year-old anti-slavery scroll which was found in a storage box at Grotonwood, the home mission of The American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts, Thursday, June 26, 2025, in Groton, Mass. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)
Rev. Diane Badger unfurls a recently found, 178-year-old anti-slavery scroll at Grotonwood, the home mission of The American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts, Thursday, June 26, 2025, in Groton, Mass. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)

Split over slavery
The document also shines a spotlight on a critical moment in the history of
the Baptist church
.
It was signed two years after the issue of slavery prompted southern Baptists to split from northern Baptists and form the
Southern Baptist Convention,
the nation’s largest Protestant denomination. The split in 1845 followed a ruling by the American Baptist Foreign Mission Society prohibiting slave owners from becoming missionaries. The northern Baptists eventually became American Baptist Churches USA.
“It comes from such a critical era in American history, you know, right prior to the Civil War,” said the Rev. Mary Day Hamel, the executive minister of the American Baptist Churches of Massachusetts.
“It was a unique moment in history when Baptists in Massachusetts stepped up and took a strong position and stood for justice in the shaping of this country,” she said. “That’s become part of our heritage to this day, to be people who stand for justice, for American Baptists to embrace diversity.”
A risky declaration
Deborah Bingham Van Broekhoven, the executive director emerita of the American Baptist Historical Society, said many Americans at the time, especially in the North, were “undecided” about slavery and weren’t sure how to respond or were worried about speaking out.
“They thought it was a southern problem, and they had no business getting involved in what they saw as the state’s rights,” Van Broekhoven said. “Most Baptists, prior to this, would have refrained from this kind of protest. This is a very good example of them going out on a limb and trying to be diplomatic.”

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了与YouTube相关的多项信息和功能。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻资讯、版权声明、联系方式、创作者相关信息、广告、开发者支持、服务条款、隐私政策、安全指南以及YouTube的运作方式和测试新功能的信息。此外，还提及了NFL Sunday Ticket服务，版权归2025年的Google LLC所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ClojureScript的编译和使用体验，包括在生产环境中的调试可行性以及对新手的入门指导。

不同观点：
• [tekacs] 分享了其在活动中的提问经历，原本想了解在ClojureScript生产环境编译中保留足够信息以实现重新激活（re-hydrating）的难度。他提到，虽然答案在他意料之中，但这确实是一个非常复杂的问题。他还提到自己目前主要使用Rust，因此短期内不会提供解决方案，并推荐了其他相关演讲。
  
• [chamomeal] 认为该视频是一个很好的ClojureScript入门介绍，并分享了自己对ClojureScript的体验。作为初学者，他觉得ClojureScript虽然很酷，但因为其拥有完整的生态系统，入门感到困惑。不过，这激发了他尝试ClojureScript的强烈兴趣，并认为它在现代web开发中仍然非常先进。

• [cjohnson318] 简短地表示他正在寻找ClojureScript材料，并感谢了相关内容的推荐。

补充讨论：
• [tekacs] 提出的技术问题涉及到ClojureScript在生产环境中调试的技术复杂性，以及潜在的解决方案。他预期在生产环境中附加一个REPL以进行调试是一个艰巨的任务，并提到自己目前主要使用Rust，暗示了两种语言在调试和开发上的不同。

• [chamomeal] 对ClojureScript的入门难度和生态系统的复杂性提出了个人看法，强调了新手在面对ClojureScript时的困惑，但也表现出了对该技术的热情和期待。

争议焦点：
• 技术实现的可行性：[tekacs] 提出的在生产环境中附加REPL以调试ClojureScript的想法，虽然技术上可能，但实现起来非常复杂，目前没有简单的解决方案。

• 入门难度：[chamomeal] 强调了ClojureScript对于新手的复杂性和入门难度，这可能是ClojureScript社区需要关注和解决的一个问题，以吸引更多开发者。

data.title: Hugging Your Cactus
data.author: ozgrakkurt
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了“拥抱仙人掌”这一比喻，源自罗伯特·唐尼在颁奖礼上介绍梅尔·吉布森时的演讲。唐尼谈到了吉布森在他困境时给予的支持和建议：不要放弃希望，找到基于宽恕的信仰，并勇于承担错误责任，拥抱自己的丑陋面（即“拥抱仙人掌”），从中学会谦卑，让生活获得新意义。文章进一步阐述了这一过程包括从羞耻、破碎到谦卑、治愈的旅程，强调不要孤立自己，要在群体中找到希望和支持。关键在于接受宽恕，既要原谅他人，也要原谅自己，从而实现真正的个人转变。拥抱仙人掌的过程虽痛苦，但通过面对和处理这些痛苦，可以获得真实的希望和人生的新意义。

不同观点：

• [0xDEAFBEAD的观点] 该评论者对文章中涉及的信仰部分表示兴趣，特别是关于不必遵循特定的宗教信仰，只要信仰 rooted in forgiveness（植根于原谅）。他们提到自己并非宗教信徒，但赞赏宗教中的救赎概念，认为世俗文化可以从宗教中学到有关救赎的价值。这显示出评论者对信仰和救赎的开放态度，同时保持非宗教立场。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点：虽然没有直接的争议，但两个评论者对信仰的看法存在微妙差异。cjcenizal更关注自我接纳和原谅的实际应用，而0xDEAFBEAD则在非宗教背景下欣赏宗教概念，特别是救赎的价值。

• 论据和例子：cjcenizal提供了个人经历作为支持，说明这些理念如何帮助他们应对生活中的困难。0xDEAFBEAD则通过引用文章中关于信仰和原谅的关系，表达了对宗教某些元素的欣赏，尽管自己并非宗教信徒。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：两个评论者都强调了原谅这一主题，但切入角度不同。cjcenizal侧重于个人应用和成长，而0xDEAFBEAD则讨论了信仰和救赎在更广泛的文化背景下的意义。

The metaphor of “hugging the cactus” originates from a speech that the actor Robert Downey gave as he was introducing his friend Mel Gibson during an award presentation.  During this time Gibson was going through some public struggles of his own and was a somewhat unexpected choice for the honor.  “To some surprise, Downey gave the gift of public acceptance to the embattled actor [Gibson]; …the defense was a return of kindness for Downey.  Gibson gave “The Avengers” actor a job in 2003’s “The Singing Detective” after his drug arrests made him uninsurable.”
[1]
With this time in mind, Downey reflected on the following advice his friend had once offered him:
Here is a link to the speech itself:
“Actually I asked Mel to present me with this reward for a reason.  When I couldn’t get sober, he told me not to give up hope, and he urged me to find my faith. It didn’t have to be his faith or anyone else’s, as long as it was rooted in forgiveness. And I couldn’t get hired, so he cast me as the lead in a movie that was actually developed for him. He kept a roof over my head, and he kept food on the table. And most importantly, he said if I accepted responsibility for my wrongdoings and if I embraced that part of my soul that was ugly — “hugging the cactus” he calls it — he said that if I “hugged the cactus” long enough, I’d become a man of some humility and that my life would take on a new meaning. And I did, and it worked. All he asked in return was that someday I help the next guy in some small way. It’s reasonable to assume that at the time he didn’t imagine that the next guy would be him or that someday was tonight.”
[2]
In this short yet powerful speech, several concepts form around this idea of hugging your cactus.  Looking at it more closely one can see the outline of a cactus hugging journey being mapped out; a journey from shame, brokenness and false or shadow self toward humility, healing, a more holistic sense of self, and ultimately a life of new meaning.  This is an invitation to deny or “die to” self or ego and is laid out in six parts that are best seen more fluidly than as rigid sequential steps.  The following brief unpacking and application of this speech has been influenced from research toward my Doctor of Ministry thesis project at Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary.
When life is not working don’t give up hope
Life, or at least a part of life not working means that something has gone wrong, perhaps even for an extended period of time.  The 12 Step tradition refers to this as “life as no longer manageable.”  One important point here is that in hugging your cactus a self-inflicted crisis is directly related to one’s life not working.  This could be a single really bad choice, a pattern of behavior, or something in between.  Whatever the reason when one realizes this, it is important not to lose or give up their hope that things can get better, that healing and an authentic personal transformation is possible.  This healing happens best in community, so here it is important for one not to isolate their self in despair, but instead find others who can be a source of hope, support, and encouragement.  It is also important here to recognize that the sense of despair and hopelessness is there for a reason. Therefore it’s also important to not move on from hopelessness too soon.  Instead, lean into it and learn from it, for the cactus hugging journey does involve dealing with pain, even self inflicted pain.  Working through despair can actually be an important part of connecting with authentic hope; however, it is also important not to stay in hopelessness too long as hope is an essential part of the cactus hugging journey.
Find a faith rooted in forgiveness
Closely related to the idea of hope in the cactus hugging journey is faith, specifically a faith that is rooted in forgiveness.  The alternative here is a faith rooted in performance or perfection, and yet, simply trying harder does not work.  Forgiveness is key in accepting that one is responsible for the crisis that has led to their life not working, and forgiveness takes practice; without forgiveness there can be no real or lasting hope.  It is also worth noting that the ability to both give and receive forgiveness are equally important here and that often the most difficult person to forgive is one’s self.
Take personal responsibility for wrongdoings
It is worth noting that accepting and taking responsibility for wrong doings is very difficult, yet this is also where real change can start to happen.  Self awareness comes into play in a strong way here as one comes to terms with their real self, the part of self that has caused harm to others.  This again is painful, yet it is why one must lean into the pain and despair, but not stay there either.  This is closely related to forgiveness, for a true sense of forgiveness actually promotes greater p

44477151.article_content:
Entertainment
How a Canadian's AI hoax duped the media and propelled a 'band' to streaming success
A Canadian who duped journalists in an elaborate hoax involving Spotify, AI and a suspicious rock band says he apologizes to anyone hurt by his experiment but that it's been "too fascinating" to turn away from.
Pretended to represent The Velvet Sundown as a 'social engineering' experiment
Kevin Maimann
·
CBC News
·
Posted: Jul 05, 2025 9:03 PM EDT | Last Updated: 3 hours ago
The Velvet Sundown uses this image as its profile photo on Spotify and social media. The band's music, which is made with artificial intelligence tools, has become the centre of an elaborate hoax.
(Facebook)
Social Sharing
A Canadian who duped journalists in an elaborate AI music hoax says he apologizes to anyone hurt by his experiment but that it's been "too fascinating" to turn away from.
A man using the pseudonym Andrew Frelon posed as the spokesperson for a band called The Velvet Sundown — which he later said he had no involvement with — creating a media frenzy that propelled the AI-assisted "band" to a million monthly listeners on Spotify.
He spoke with CBC News over the phone Friday on condition that his real name not be revealed. CBC News agreed not to use his real name because he fears harassment based on the hateful messages he's received online, and worries he would lose work if identified.
The sticky online saga began when the band appeared on music streaming platforms several weeks ago and amassed hundreds of thousands of streams from two full-length albums.
Its blend of laid-back 1970s-inspired rock and modern indie pop appeared on several popular Spotify playlists, including one featuring Vietnam War songs.
Commotion
Timbaland used an independent producer's work to train AI — but without the artist's consent
AI song sparks debate in Francophone music scene
But savvy listeners noticed something was off. The band's supposed members had no digital footprint, and there was no record of them ever having performed live. The album art and profile photo, featuring four shaggy-haired rockers, also carried hallmarks of generative AI.
But as the controversy gained steam, an account on
social media platform X
purporting to represent the band emphatically denied that any of the music was created by artificial intelligence, calling the accusations "lazy" and "baseless."
CBC reached out to the X account on Wednesday and attempted to arrange an interview through a Gmail account purporting to represent the band.
Then, a man calling himself Andrew Frelon
told Rolling Stone
, in an article that was published online later that day, that he is behind The Velvet Sundown and the X account, and that he used generative AI platform Suno to create the songs. He called the project an "art hoax."
WATCH | Expert speaks on AI regulation:
Why more needs to be done to regulate the use of AI
1 year ago
Duration
6:07
New research out of Western University is shining a light on the federal government's use of artificial intelligence through a Tracking Automated Government Register. Joanna Redden, an associate professor of Information and Media Studies and co-director at Starling: Just Technologies. Just Societies. and Data Justice Lab, joined London Morning to talk about the data and concerns about AI use.
But just as the mystery appeared to be solved, a different X account linked to the official Velvet Sundown Spotify page
posted a statement
saying Frelon has nothing to do with the band.
"Someone is attempting to hijack the identity of The Velvet Sundown," said the statement, which also appeared on the band's Spotify and Instagram accounts on Thursday.
That same day, Frelon, who gave the Rolling Stone interview,
posted a lengthy blog
confirming he had nothing to do with the band and that nearly everything he told the magazine, including his name, was a lie.
The actual band's identity was once again a mystery. It turned out the hoax was, in fact, part of a bigger hoax.
'It's too fascinating of a mystery'
Speaking with CBC News on Friday, Frelon maintained that he has "zero" connection to the Velvet Sundown.
Asked about his motivation for maintaining such a complicated ruse, Frelon said the way the whole thing has played out has become like "artistic jet fuel."
"There's so many weird cultural, technical things at play here. It's too fascinating of a mystery for me to turn away from," he said.
The real person behind Andrew Frelon is an expert on web platform safety and policy issues, with extensive experience using generative AI. He was born in the United States but lives in Canada.
A man calling himself Andrew Frelon says he used AI to generate this image of The Velvet Sundown.
(Andrew Frelon)
Several major American publications have interviewed him about his other AI projects and safety and policy issues work.
CBC News verified his identity through screen shots and a Signal video chat. Frelon sent screen shots of his correspondence with Rolling Stone to confirm

data.title: Ask HN: Advice for Starting a Hacker Space?
data.author: pkdpic
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何成功运营创客空间/黑客空间，包括工具组织、财务管理、成员行为规范、社区建设等方面。

不同观点：
• [dv35z] 认为该书是创建成功创客空间的“黄金标准”，涵盖了工具组织、人员配置、标准操作流程、敏捷方法、创业精神、资金等多个方面，是高度推荐的指南。

• [bsenftner] 基于创办和运营Droplabs的经验，强调需要将所有成员的期望和行为边界书面化，特别是财务义务和违规处罚，并指出共享空间容易引发问题，尤其是涉及财务时。同时建议决策一旦做出，不应无休止地争论。

• [CursedSilicon] 对[bsenftner]的观点提出质疑，指出西雅图的不同创客空间情况有所不同，认为社区建设和积极氛围的维持更为重要。

• [jerkstate] 区分了社区创客空间和商业创客空间的运营问题，指出社区空间规模较小，问题相对简单，主要集中在成员行为和组织活动上，并建议建立入会流程和责任豁免书，以减少法律风险。同时提到利用LLMs设计学习活动和保持空间学习氛围的重要性。

• [yummypaint] 补充了关于电子废物回收作为获取廉价或免费材料的渠道的建议，特别适用于教导孩子进行零件 salvaging 和再利用。

• [mandeepj] 指出开始时购买设备可能需要大量资金，除非专注于非常特定的 niche。

• [kulahan] 建议可以与当地图书馆合作，或通过捐赠主要工具与图书馆建立联系。

• [threatofrain] 认为如果只是在车库里为一小群孩子举办计算机俱乐部，不需要太多复杂的规划和管理。

• [MongooseStudios] 简单表示对该想法的支持，没有提供具体建议。

• [cranberryturkey] 开玩笑地提到如果有资金，会考虑在底特律购买便宜房屋并改造成黑客空间。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于运营创客空间时问题的复杂性和规模，尤其是社区空间与商业空间的对比，以及如何有效管理成员行为和财务问题。
• 强调书面化规则和行为边界的重要性，以减少潜在冲突和法律风险。
• 提出利用电子废物回收作为获取材料的渠道，以及设计学习活动以保持空间学习氛围的具体建议。
• 不同空间的具体情况（如西雅图 vs. 其他地区）可能影响运营策略。

总结：评论主要围绕创客空间运营的实际问题展开，包括工具组织、财务管理、成员行为规范和社区建设等方面，提供了书面化规则、利用电子废物回收、与图书馆合作等具体建议，并区分了社区空间和商业空间的运营差异。

data.title: Tesla opens 168 stall Supercharger station, with solar farm and big batteries
data.author: decimalenough
data.article_summary: Tesla在加州Lost Hills开设了一个大型超级充电站，占地30英亩，目前有84个充电桩投入使用，最终将扩展至168个，成为世界上最大的充电站。该站点配备11兆瓦的太阳能阵列，包括太阳能遮阳棚和邻近的太阳能农场，以及10个Tesla Megapack电池，完全由太阳能供电并可离网运行。每个V4超级充电桩功率为325千瓦，其中12个为可直接通过的设计，方便拖挂车或船只的电动车主充电。该站点位于I-5州际公路旁，是全球最繁忙的电动车走廊之一，预计剩余的充电桩和休息区将在今年圣诞节前开放。充电费用为每千瓦时0.62美元，对所有使用北美充电标准（NACS）插头的电动车开放。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：充电站的布局及收费标准是否合理

不同观点：
• Rebelgecko认为充电站布局稀疏但每个站点有更多充电桩是更好的选择。他觉得这种布局虽然有些反直觉，但可能是更优的方案。
• 对于充电费用（60¢+/kWh），Rebelgecko表达了对回本时间的担忧，暗示当前的收费标准可能偏高，导致回本周期较长。

补充讨论：
• 关于充电站布局的讨论中，存在不同偏好。有人可能认为密集的充电站布局更方便用户使用，而另一些人如Rebelgecko则倾向于更广分布但每个站点拥有更多充电桩的布局。
• 收费标准问题引发了对经济性的关注，60¢+/kWh的收费水平是否合理，取决于充电需求和竞争对手的定价，同时也关系到充电站的运营成本和回本速度。
• 争议焦点在于充电站的布局和收费标准的平衡：如何在用户便利性和经济效益之间找到最佳的解决方案。

Last week, The Driven reported on Tesla opening its latest Supercharger station in Australia, which features the country’s largest solar canopy to with an 80 kW solar array.
Now, the company has shared news of a behemoth site in the US, with 11 MW of solar array – both in the solar canopy and a neighbouring solar farm, along with 10 Tesla Megapack batteries. So far, 84 stalls of supercharging are open to the public in Lost Hills, California.
Image: Tesla
The site is located on Interstate 5 between San Francisco & Los Angeles, which, according to Tesla, is one of the busiest EV corridors in the world.
This site is expected to eventually have up to 168 V4 supercharger stalls when fully commissioned, making it one of the biggest charging sites in the world.
On Tesla Charging’s X page, the company shared the opening of the new site, which took around 8 months to complete, just in time for the Fourth of July holidays when tens of thousands of EVs are expected to be on the move.

July 3, 2025
On Tesla’s website, the site can be accessed between 10 am and 8 pm every day with base rate charging for EVs set art $US0.62 per kWh. It’s also open to all EVs that can charge using a NACS (North America Charging Standard) plug.
It also shows that each of the V4 supercharger stalls are rated at 325 kW, although the charging speeds at each stall may vary.
A breakdown of what’s on the ground was also shared by EV news aggregator Sawyerr Merritt on X, which highlights that the site is on 30 acres of land.
12 of the 84 stalls are pull-through which means EV drivers towing trailers, caravans, or boats won’t need to unhitch before charging.
The remainder of the 168 stalls will open later this year, ahead of the Christmas holidays in December.
NEWS: Tesla has officially opened one of the largest Superchargers in the world in California. Later this year, it will be THE biggest in the world.
• 168 stall Supercharger (84 stalls open now, rest later this year)
• 11 MW of ground mount solar & canopies, on 30 acres of…
https://t.co/r8hakM7KY6
pic.twitter.com/GQPNfprnGN
— Sawyer Merritt (@SawyerMerritt)
July 3, 2025
According to Max de Zegher, who heads up charging at Tesla, the site is initially running off a 1.5 MW feed but is expected to expand with grid capacity availability and site charging demand.
The opening of this site comes only days after the company announced that it had installed its 70,000th supercharger stall globally with the opening of its new 12-stall site in Burleson, Texas.
That news came just 8 months after the company rolled out its 60,000th supercharger stall, which was located in Enshu Morimachi, Japan, in 2024.
Image: Tesla
With EV adoption at an all-time high, it’s great to see Tesla continuing to expand the world’s most reliable fast charging network.
The expansion is also continuing here in Australia with new sites opening every month, alongside expansion and upgrades to existing sites. That’s also going to provide confidence to current and future EV owners to make the switch to cleaner EVs sooner.

data.article_summary: Volvo Trucks已悄然交付第5,000辆电动半挂卡车，自2019年推出首辆全电动卡车以来，其电动卡车已在50多个国家运行超过1.7亿公里，大幅减少二氧化碳和氮氧化物排放以及交通噪音。尽管特斯拉Semi频繁成为头条新闻，但目前上路的数量仅约140辆，而Volvo凭借更早的起步和广泛的市场部署，在欧洲电动重卡市场占据了47%的份额。Volvo的电动卡车系列包括多款车型，满足不同运输需求，且公司高管对未来增长充满信心。尽管特斯拉曾在其他领域超越老牌车企，但在电动卡车领域，Volvo已建立显著领先优势。

Commercial EVs
Electric Semi Truck
Volvo Trucks
Volvo delivers 5,000th electric semi with little fanfare, sending a BIG message
Jo Borrás
| Jun 29 2025 - 12:18 pm PT
117 Comments
With the Tesla Semi making headlines consistently since its first public appearance
waaay
back back in 2017, you might think they were some kind of market leaders. Meanwhile, Volvo Trucks has quietly delivered its 5,000th electric semi truck … and they’re just getting started.
Volvo delivered its first all electric semi truck 2019. Since then,
Volvo customers in more than 50 countries around the world have logged more than 100
million
miles
(170 million km –
and almost half of that in the last 14 months as the size of its deployed fleet grows
) in real-world commercial operations, eliminating massive amounts of CO
2
and NOx emissions and reducing traffic noise. All the while, they’re making life a little cleaner and quieter for the people who live and work near the roads they travel.
They’re massive achievements, and Volvo Truck executives are very rightly proud of themselves for making them happen.
“It’s rewarding to see that transport companies continue to embrace the benefits with electric trucks in a wide range of transport segments,” offers Roger Alm, President Volvo Trucks. “Volvo’s battery-electric trucks are available here and now, providing our customers and transport buyers with a more sustainable alternative that makes business sense, and many of our customers are coming back to us to grow their electric fleets.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
King of the electric road
VNR Electric; via Volvo Trucks.
They say comparison is the thief of joy. That’s especially true if you suck and you compare yourself to people who are awesome –
and since Elon sucks like it’s his job
, I’m thieving a ton of joy by comparing the 140-odd number of Tesla Semi trucks out there to Volvo’s much larger, less-sucky 5,000-plus number.
With a head start like that, more than half a decade of production delays, and a “
dramatic
” price increase to something like $420,000 each, it seems like it would be tough for Tesla to catch up (
even if they
do
manage to begin series production in 2026
).
That seems especially true in Europe, where Volvo Trucks has established itself as the leader in the heavy electric truck segment for the last five consecutive years with a 47% market share – though the story is a bit different the US and Canada, however, where Volvo’s share of the electric truck segment was “just” 40% in 2024.
Volvo Trucks electric lineup
Volvo FL Electric
Volvo FE Electric
Volvo FM Electric
Volvo FM Low Entry
Volvo FMX Electric
Volvo FH Electric
Volvo FH Aero Electric
Volvo VNR Electric
Top comment by
Rob Guerney
Liked by 23 people
I really think the Tesla Semi, might have a major design flaw and might not be able to get enough weight on the steer axle and too much on the drives. Trucks have to make axle weight as well as gross weight, and i know electric trucks get an extra 2000 lbs. Tesla has a lot of empty space towards the front axle. Photos Initially show the frunk empty. Now they have moved the HVAC system to the frunk apparently to get some weight up there.  So I would guess the original design had no consideration of axle weight, which is a mistake legacy truck builders wouldn't make because on diesel trucks they  place the fuel tanks and batteries to get proper weight distribution. It depends on how far Tesla can move the batteries forward but the walk in cab might prevent that. In the the drawings with a see-through cab it looks like the batteries are forward, but it also looks like the batteries are where the walk in door us supposed to be. Diesels obviously have the weight of the engine up there Just look at a European Cabovers to see how much they put ahead of the front axle, this helps get the weight up. I'm guessing Tesla went for the "Wouldn't it be neat to have a walk in cab" look as opposed to the considerations of the real world of trucking. Of course all this is a guess since Tesla won't release the weights.
View all comments
That said, Tesla has beaten legacy brands with massive, seemingly insurmountable leads before – but the good news is that,
when it comes to EVs
, whoever wins, we kind of all win, you know? Even Elon! That’s my take, anyway. Head down to the comments and let me know yours.

data.title: Busting the top myths about the Big Bang
data.author: VignuB
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了大爆炸理论，并澄清了关于该理论的五大误解。大爆炸并非一次巨大的爆炸，而是宇宙从高温、高密度的状态开始膨胀和冷却的过程。文章解释了哈勃定律，描述了宇宙膨胀导致星系光谱红移的现象，并指出这并不意味着所有星系都从一个点爆炸产生。宇宙在138亿年前从炽热致密的状态开始，不断膨胀和冷却，但大爆炸本身并不是通常认为的一次性事件。文章还提到宇宙的年龄有限，因此我们只能看到一定距离内的星系，即使使用最先进的望远镜如JWST，最远的星系也只能追溯到宇宙诞生后2.8亿年。文章最后强调，理解这些科学真相有助于纠正人们对大爆炸的误解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宇宙的定义和大爆炸理论中空间的边界问题

不同观点：
• Fracus认为，将大爆炸理论与普通人理解的概念联系起来的主要问题在于空间的定义。他质疑在没有已知边界的情况下如何定义空间，并提出宇宙如果没有明确边界，那么如何确定没有中心点。他使用了一个烤面包膨胀的类比，指出即使是面包也有质量中心，而宇宙如果没有定义边界，那该如何理解。

• Fracus进一步质疑，宇宙之外的空间应该如何定义，并提出了一个思想实验：如果在星系间取一个盒子并抽成没有任何质量和能量的真空，那么这种“虚无”是否与宇宙外的“虚无”相同。他认为，这类似于理查德·费曼在解释科学原理时遇到的“为什么”难题，即用简单的类比解释科学概念时总有不完美之处。

补充讨论：
• 提到了用类比解释科学概念的局限性，尤其是像宇宙边界和空间定义这样复杂的概念。Fracus指出，任何试图用简单的类比（如ELI5，即“解释给我听就像我五岁一样”）来解释这些概念，都会有不一致的地方，而进一步的解释又会过于复杂。

• 评论中隐含的争议焦点在于如何有效地向公众解释复杂的科学概念，尤其是那些涉及抽象和难以直观理解的主题，如宇宙的边界和空间的定义。

44477166.article_content:
At the start of the hot Big Bang, the Universe was rapidly expanding and filled with high-energy, very densely packed, ultra-relativistic quanta. An early stage of radiation domination gave way to several later stages where radiation was sub-dominant, but never went away completely, while matter then clumped into gas clouds, stars, star clusters, galaxies, and even richer structures over time, all while the Universe continues expanding. The time after the relic radiation has faded away but before stars have ignited marks the cosmic dark ages.
Credit
: CfA/M. Weiss
Key Takeaways
The Big Bang is something that most people have heard of, with the understanding that it is the leading theory of our cosmic origins: well established for over 60 years.
However, many people hold an enormous number of misconceptions about what the Big Bang is, driven on not only by popular narratives, but also by science contrarians who seek to undermine our carefully collected, bona fide knowledge.
These are the top five myths that cosmologists commonly hear regarding the hot Big Bang, and rebuttals with windows into the actual truths of what we know and how we know it.
Ethan Siegel
Copy a link to the article entitled http://Busting%20the%20top%205%20myths%20about%20the%20Big%20Bang

Travel the universe with Dr. Ethan Siegel as he answers the biggest questions of all.
Subscribe
The Universe we know today, filled with stars and galaxies across the great cosmic abyss, hasn’t been around forever. Despite the fact that there are several trillions of galaxies visible to us, spanning distances of tens of billions of light-years, there’s a limit to how far away we can look. Even here in the JWST era, the most distant galaxy we’ve ever seen is located an impressive 34 billion light-years away, with its light corresponding to a time where the Universe was a mere 280 million years old: just 2% of its current age. Why can’t we see farther than that? The reason isn’t because the Universe is finite — in fact, it may well be infinite after all — but rather because it had a beginning that occurred a finite amount of time ago: the Big Bang.
The fact that we can:
look at our Universe today,
see it expanding and cooling,
and infer our cosmic origins from what we observe,
is one of the most profound scientific achievements of the 20th century. The Universe began from a hot, dense, matter-and-radiation filled state some 13.8 billion years ago, and has been expanding, cooling, and gravitating ever since. But the Big Bang itself doesn’t work the way most people think. Here are the top 5 myths that people believe about the Big Bang, along with the science behind what’s actually true instead.
This rare color photo shows the first nuclear explosion at the Trinity Site in New Mexico on July 16, 1945. This nuclear detonation ushered humanity into the Atomic Age, with the fireball rising 200 meters into the air a mere 16 milliseconds after detonation. If it weren’t for the presence of the ground or the heat-induced airflow of the mushroom cloud, the explosion would appear as a nearly perfectly-symmetric sphere.
Credit
: National Nuclear Security Administration / Public domain
1.) The Big Bang is the explosion that began our Universe
. Every time we look out at a distant galaxy in the Universe and try to measure what its light is doing, we see the same pattern emerge: the farther away the galaxy is, the more significantly its light is systematically shifted to longer and longer wavelengths. This redshift that we observe for these objects follows a predictable pattern, with double the distance meaning that the light’s wavelength will be shifted by twice as great an amount. The farther away we look, the greater an object’s redshift, indicating that it appears to be receding from us at a much faster speed.
This is what’s encoded in
Hubble’s Law
(or the Hubble-Lemaître Law): a relationship between the inferred recession speed of a distant object and its measured distance from us, with the Hubble constant indicating the rate of recession as a function of distance. Just as a police car speeding away from you will sound lower-pitched the faster it moves away from you, the greater we measure an object’s distance to be from us, the greater the measured redshift of its light will be. It makes a lot of sense, then, to think that the more distant objects are moving away from us at faster speeds, and that we could trace every galaxy we see today back to a single point in the past: an enormous explosion.
The ‘raisin bread’ model of the expanding Universe, where relative distances increase as the space (dough) expands. The farther away any two raisins are from one another, the greater the observed redshift will be by the time the light is received.
44477166.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了大爆炸理论，并澄清了关于该理论的五大误解。大爆炸并非一次巨大的爆炸，而是宇宙从高温、高密度的状态开始膨胀和冷却的过程。文章解释了哈勃定律，描述了宇宙膨胀导致星系光谱红移的现象，并指出这并不意味着所有星系都从一个点爆炸产生。宇宙在138亿年前从炽热致密的状态开始，不断膨胀和冷却，但大爆炸本身并不是通常认为的一次性事件。文章还提到宇宙的年龄有限，因此我们只能看到一定距离内的星系，即使使用最先进的望远镜如JWST，最远的星系也只能追溯到宇宙诞生后2.8亿年。文章最后强调，理解这些科学真相有助于纠正人们对大爆炸的误解。
44477166.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宇宙的定义和大爆炸理论中空间的边界问题

不同观点：
• Fracus认为，将大爆炸理论与普通人理解的概念联系起来的主要问题在于空间的定义。他质疑在没有已知边界的情况下如何定义空间，并提出宇宙如果没有明确边界，那么如何确定没有中心点。他使用了一个烤面包膨胀的类比，指出即使是面包也有质量中心，而宇宙如果没有定义边界，那该如何理解。

• Fracus进一步质疑，宇宙之外的空间应该如何定义，并提出了一个思想实验：如果在星系间取一个盒子并抽成没有任何质量和能量的真空，那么这种“虚无”是否与宇宙外的“虚无”相同。他认为，这类似于理查德·费曼在解释科学原理时遇到的“为什么”难题，即用简单的类比解释科学概念时总有不完美之处。

补充讨论：
• 提到了用类比解释科学概念的局限性，尤其是像宇宙边界和空间定义这样复杂的概念。Fracus指出，任何试图用简单的类比（如ELI5，即“解释给我听就像我五岁一样”）来解释这些概念，都会有不一致的地方，而进一步的解释又会过于复杂。

• 评论中隐含的争议焦点在于如何有效地向公众解释复杂的科学概念，尤其是那些涉及抽象和难以直观理解的主题，如宇宙的边界和空间的定义。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕数据可视化工具kepler.gl及其相关开源项目的讨论，包括社区贡献、实际应用价值和替代方案。

不同观点：
• **支持并推广相关项目**：
  - [loicsaintroch] 分享了自己基于kepler.gl和DuckDB构建的开源地图编辑器，并提供了项目链接供他人参考，展示了kepler.gl的实际应用。
  - [pininja] 鼓励社区贡献者参加即将在西雅图举办的协作峰会，并提到kepler.gl的创始人和其他相关项目的创建者将出席会议，显示出对社区活动的支持。
  - [adeptima] 提到Foursquare的另一个开源项目SQLRooms，强调了DuckDB在数据可视化领域的多个项目之间的关联性。
  - [ppage] 表达了对kepler.gl的喜爱，并提到自己经常用它来可视化行程，显示出对该工具的实际应用支持。

• **技术工具的关联性**：
  - [qwertox] 指出kepler.gl所依赖的另一个库deck.gl，强调了这些技术工具之间的相互关联性。

• **对实际应用价值的质疑**：
  - [zkmon] 对kepler.gl等可视化工具的实际决策价值提出质疑，认为复杂的可视化在实际决策中往往不如简单的文本或数字有效，表达了对这类工具实际应用效果的怀疑。

• **商业替代方案的问题**：
  - [aidanlister] 对CARTO的高昂和不透明的定价表示不满，认为kepler.gl是其一个很好的替代方案，显示了对开源工具在经济性和透明度方面的偏好。

补充讨论：
• **历史背景**：
  - [peterb] 提供了kepler.gl在2018年的发布链接，帮助新参与者了解该工具的历史背景。

• **具体应用场景**：
  - [xyst] 提到kepler.gl在移动端的使用体验有待改进，并提出了一个具体的应用场景，即通过手机GPS数据生成热力图，展示了kepler.gl在个人数据可视化中的潜力。

争议焦点：
• **可视化工具的实际决策价值**：[zkmon] 对kepler.gl等复杂可视化工具在实际决策中的有效性提出质疑，与其他支持者形成对比。

data.title: Killer whales groom each other with pieces of kelp
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于虎鲸（或称为杀人鲸）的行为及其名称的讨论

不同观点：
• robaato认为文章有趣，提到虎鲸用海带茎相互按摩，将其与海豚的表演性行为相比较，带有些许调侃意味。
• metalman补充虎鲸会分享食物，甚至提到野生虎鲸会将食物扔向人类，以观察人类的行为，表现出对这一现象的惊叹。
• bmitc建议将“Killer whales”改为“Orcas”，认为名称应更符合虎鲸的科学分类。
• fuzzfactor以幽默的方式回应虎鲸相互梳理的行为，提出如果它们不这么做，那谁会来做。
• wiether作为英语非母语者，表达了对“Killer whales”这一名称的不适感，认为“whales”不符合其科学分类，且“killer”会引发不必要的恐惧。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及虎鲸的智力和社会行为，如分享食物和使用工具（海带），这些行为显示了它们的复杂性和社会性。
• 名称争议是另一个讨论焦点，bmitc和wiether都对“Killer whales”这一名称提出了质疑，认为“Orcas”更为合适，并指出名称可能带来的偏见和误解。
• metalman的观点中还包含了对虎鲸与人类互动的观察，强调了虎鲸在自然环境中的主动行为，而非人为训练的结果。

争议焦点：
• 虎鲸名称的适当性：“Killer whales” vs. “Orcas”。
• 对虎鲸行为的解读，尤其是其与人类互动和使用工具的行为，是否应视为具有某种智力和社会性。

data.title: Launch HN: K-Scale Labs (YC W24) – Open-Source Humanoid Robots
data.author: codekansas
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款开源人形机器人的发布引发的技术、市场和伦理讨论

不同观点：
• **对开源和已有项目的质疑**：BrandiATMuhkuh提出疑问，为什么选择从头构建而不是基于ROS等现有开源项目。他认为可能需要一次“重启”，并对两足机器人的稳定性表示怀疑。
• **对机器人足部设计的讨论**：chrsw关注 humanoid机器人缺少人类足部的关键关节和感知能力，质疑这种设计对机器人移动性能的影响。
• **价格和市场定位的争议**：fragmede和deepdarkforest都提到了价格问题，fragmede对比了不同型号的价格差异，而deepdarkforest则对当前售价和未来承诺的全自动功能之间的不确定性表示担忧，将其比作特斯拉的FSD问题。
• **机器人的实际应用场景**：srameshc和markisus关注机器人的实际应用和市场前景，质疑其目前是否解决了实际问题，以及如何向投资人解释其商业价值。
• **技术实现和自主性**：randomNumber7和dbmikus对机器人全自主性的技术实现表示关注，特别是机器学习算法的应用以及物理硬件和仿真环境之间的平衡。

补充讨论：
• **伦理和未来风险**：999900000999提出了对该技术被不当使用或军事化的担忧，并将其与科幻电影中的情节相比较。同时，还提出了对AGI机器人道德问题的疑虑。
• **硬件设计的现实挑战**：Mars008对机器人在真实环境中的行走能力表示怀疑，认为仿真训练可能不足以保证可靠性。
• **对机器人手部设计的关注**：lachyg询问了目前最好用的机械手设计，并期待价格合理且性能可靠的五指手。
• **其他小问题**：bbor指出了网站链接404错误的问题，v5v3则质疑了市场对女性化设计和“易清洁”特性的关注。

争议的焦点：
• **两足设计与四足设计的优劣**：对两足机器人稳定性的质疑与其他设计选择之间的争议。
• **价格与价值**：当前定价是否合理，尤其是考虑到未来可能实现的全自主功能，市场接受度存在争议。
• **伦理与安全**：技术的潜在军事化应用和道德问题引发了讨论。

总的来说，讨论涵盖了技术实现、市场前景、伦理问题以及设计细节等多方面内容，展现了对人形机器人未来发展的多角度思考。

data.title: Sleeping beauty Bitcoin wallets wake up after 14 years to the tune of $2B
data.author: aorloff
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：比特币的现状、巨额比特币资产的处理、早期比特币参与者的经历及安全问题

不同观点：
• Synaesthesia认为比特币最初被期望成为金融革命，但现在却变成了投机工具，充斥着骗局，令他感到失望，质疑比特币现今对世界的实际价值。
• mattlondon开玩笑说可能有人正在通过大量计算资源暴力破解旧钱包的密钥，暗示对可能存在的幕后操作持怀疑态度。
• creatonez纠正关于比特币早期发展的时间线，指出中本聪在2010年已经离开，且在2011年已有大量外部交易，反驳所谓“中本聪时代”的观点。
• duttish提醒拥有巨额比特币的人要小心安全，提到“扳手攻击”（物理威胁）的增加，强调保护隐私和安全的重要性。

补充讨论：
• jedberg质疑将价值80亿美元的比特币兑换成法定货币的可行性，关注市场流动性和实际操作性。
• andy99指出市场对大额交易的敏感性，认为比特币由于其相对较小的市场深度更容易受到影响。
• ProllyInfamous提供了一些有趣的比较，指出比特币市值大于某些贵金属，并列出几家市值超过比特币的上市公司。
• cedws猜测中本聪的财富可能已经永远消失，甚至推测CIA可能已经找到其身份并控制了其密钥，暗示可能的市场影响。
• coolspot和throw0101d提到了一些具体的事件和资源链接，如某人出狱和比特币地址的公开信息。
• sizzle分享了自己早期参与比特币挖矿的经历，认为当时比特币价值低且被视为浪费资源，反映了一些早期参与者的看法。
• ksynwa询问如果拥有巨额比特币，如何兑现及具体操作的复杂性，表现出对实际操作缺乏了解。
• msgodel幽默地提到Martin Shkreli退出直播是否与破解比特币钱包有关，暗示对名人参与的猜测。
• alecsm表达了对早期丢失比特币的遗憾，反映了许多早期挖矿者因未重视比特币而错失财富的普遍现象。

争议焦点：
• 比特币的实际价值和其当前对世界的贡献存在争议，Synaesthesia对此持批评态度。
• 拥有巨额比特币的实际兑现能力和市场影响存在疑问，jedberg和andy99对此有不同看法。
• 早期比特币参与者对错过机会的遗憾和反思，如alecsm和sizzle的经历。

• mattlondon开玩笑说可能有人正在通过大量计算资源暴力破解旧钱包的密钥，暗示对可能存在的幕后操作持怀疑态度。
• creatonez纠正关于比特币早期发展的时间线，指出中本聪在2010年已经离开，且在2011年已有大量外部交易，反驳所谓“中本聪时代”的观点。
• duttish提醒拥有巨额比特币的人要小心安全，提到“扳手攻击”（物理威胁）的增加，强调保护隐私和安全的重要性。

补充讨论：
• jedberg质疑将价值80亿美元的比特币兑换成法定货币的可行性，关注市场流动性和实际操作性。
• andy99指出市场对大额交易的敏感性，认为比特币由于其相对较小的市场深度更容易受到影响。
• ProllyInfamous提供了一些有趣的比较，指出比特币市值大于某些贵金属，并列出几家市值超过比特币的上市公司。
• cedws猜测中本聪的财富可能已经永远消失，甚至推测CIA可能已经找到其身份并控制了其密钥，暗示可能的市场影响。
• coolspot和throw0101d提到了一些具体的事件和资源链接，如某人出狱和比特币地址的公开信息。
• sizzle分享了自己早期参与比特币挖矿的经历，认为当时比特币价值低且被视为浪费资源，反映了一些早期参与者的看法。
• ksynwa询问如果拥有巨额比特币，如何兑现及具体操作的复杂性，表现出对实际操作缺乏了解。
• msgodel幽默地提到Martin Shkreli退出直播是否与破解比特币钱包有关，暗示对名人参与的猜测。
• alecsm表达了对早期丢失比特币的遗憾，反映了许多早期挖矿者因未重视比特币而错失财富的普遍现象。

争议焦点：
• 比特币的实际价值和其当前对世界的贡献存在争议，Synaesthesia对此持批评态度。
• 拥有巨额比特币的实际兑现能力和市场影响存在疑问，jedberg和andy99对此有不同看法。
• 早期比特币参与者对错过机会的遗憾和反思，如alecsm和sizzle的经历。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对现代消费和服务中各种现象的批评和反思

不同观点：
• **ggm**：批评了航空公司常旅客计划的贬值，尤其是当所有人都支付额外费用时，原本的“特权”不再有优势。同时提到对Uber的厌恶，但承认已经习惯其存在。对小费文化的引入感到不满，认为不符合澳大利亚的文化。
• **hardwaresofton**：质疑政府为每个人开设投资账户的建议，认为这只会使大公司受益，并批评全民基本收入（UBI）是承认经济缺乏活力，默认许多人无法找到有尊严的工作。
• **afiodorov**：强调人们对被操纵的感知和反应——通过“数字排毒”、减少使用智能手机等方式进行“脱离”。
• **bravesoul2**：支持减少垄断企业的影响，赞赏通过支持竞争对手来打破垄断的行为。
• **cadamsdotcom**：选择退出科技产品带来的操纵，如卖掉电视、驾驶老旧汽车，等待市场出现更多以客户为中心的产品。
• **8f2ab37a-ed6c**：关注约会应用程序的禁令问题，指出被错误禁言后重新加入的困难，认为这是“反乌托邦”的。
• **protocolture**：不同意“市场会自动修复问题”的观点，指出人们仍然可以在现实中交往，约会应用程序并非唯一选择。
• **anon7000**：批评网站Fandom的广告泛滥问题，认为公司决策层和员工不应容忍这种对用户不友好的体验。
• **notarobot123**：批评算法对选择的控制，但仍相信有可能通过改变协议和激励结构，创建一个更友好的社交互联网。
• **emsign**：表达了对算法控制的强烈反感，希望脱离被公司和政府操纵的社会。

补充讨论：
• **skocznymroczny**：指出在线约会网站对大多数男性而言是浪费时间，因为只有极少数男性能获得多数女性的关注，而“提升”系统进一步加剧了这种不平衡。

争议焦点：
• 对科技产品和服务的矛盾态度：如对Uber的厌恶但接受其存在，对算法和广告的强烈反感但仍在使用相关服务。
• 市场是否能够自动修复问题：一些人认为最终会有更好的选择出现，而另一些人则认为当前的操纵和不友好体验是无法接受的，需要立即改变。

44478115.article_content:
I signed up for Hinge. Holy shit with the boosts.
How does someone who works on this wake up every morning and feel okay about themselves?
Similarly with the tip screens, Uber algorithm, all the zero sum bullshit using all the tricks of psychology to extract a little bit more from every interaction in society. Nudge. Nudge. NUDGE.
Want to partake in normal society like buying a coffee, going on a date, getting a ride, paying a friend. Oh, there’s a middle man now. An evil ominous middleman using state of the art AI algorithms to extract just a little bit more from you.
But eventually the market will fix this, right? People will feel sick of being manipulated and move elsewhere?
Ahhh, but they see that coming long before you do. They have dashboards. Quick Jeeves, tune the AI to make people
feel
less manipulated. Give them a little bit more for now, we have to think about maximizing
lifetime customer value
here.
Oh the AI already did this on its own? Jeeves you’ve been replaced! People perpetually on the edge.
You want to opt out of this all you say? Good luck running a competitive business! Every metric is now a target. You better maximize engagement or you will
lose
engagement this is a
red queen’s race
we can’t afford to lose! Burn all the social capital, burn all your values, FEED IT ALL TO MOLOCH!
Someday, people will have to realize we live in a society. What will it take? A complete self cannibalization to the point you can’t eat your own mouth? It sure as hell isn’t going to be people opting out, that’s a collective action problem you can’t solve.
Democracy, haha, you think the algorithms will let you vote to kill them? Your vote is as decoupled from action as the amount Uber pays the driver is decoupled from the fare that you pay. There’s no reform here, there’s only revolution.
Will it simply be a huge financial collapse? Or do we need World War 3? And even World War 3 is on a spectrum. Will mass starvation fix this? Or will the attitude of thinking it’s okay to manipulate others at scale persist even past
that
? He’s got his, and I’ve got mine…
If you open a government S&P 500 account for everyone with $1,000 at birth that’ll pay their social security cause it like…goes up…wait who’s creating this value again?
It’s not okay. Advertising is not okay. Price discrimination is not okay. Using big data, machine learning, and psychology to manipulate others at scale is not okay.
But you aren’t going to learn this lesson until you have fed a huge majority of your
customers
to Moloch. Modern capitialism is wireheading. Release the hypnodrones. How many cans of Pepsi did you want them to consume an hour again?

data.title: July 5, 1687: When Newton explained why you don't float away
data.author: TMEHpodcast
data.article_summary: 《宇宙变得有序的那一天（ mostly ）》讲述了牛顿在1687年7月5日发表了《自然哲学的数学原理》，解释了宇宙为何保持有序，包括苹果为何落地、行星为何不偏离轨道等现象。这本书差点未能出版，幸亏天文学家哈雷资助了印刷。自那以来，牛顿的理论被用于建造桥梁、计算行星轨道以及解释日常生活现象，如烤面包总是黄油面朝下着地。NASA至今仍使用牛顿的框架发射卫星和进行太空任务。牛顿的定律为我们提供了一个大致可预测的宇宙，使许多现代科技成为可能，尽管物理学生在考试时可能仍会抱怨他的理论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕牛顿的《自然哲学的数学原理》（Principia）的历史背景、科学贡献以及其内容的解读和评价。

不同观点：
• dr_dshiv认为牛顿在《Principia》的附录中描述了电磁学以及电振荡在神经系统中的作用，并将其与现代所谓的"vibes"（感觉）联系起来。他引用了牛顿的原文，指出牛顿描述了一种微妙的“精神”力量，解释了物体之间的吸引力、电作用、光的传播以及感觉的激发和动物身体的运动。

• progre关注《Principia》出版的资金问题，指出该书是由哈雷（Edmund Halley）资助的，因为皇家学会（Royal Academy）由于之前的出版项目《The history of fishes》失败而资金短缺。此外，即使在哈雷自己也缺钱的时候，皇家学会仍未能支付他薪水，而是给了他一些《The history of fishes》的副本。

• roenxi对牛顿的贡献持保留态度，认为虽然牛顿对物体下落提供了精确的描述和计算方法，但从基础物理的角度来看，我们仍然只是在“东西因为它们确实会掉下来而掉下来”这一现象上增加了精确性，并没有从根本上改变对这一现象的理解。

• Simon_O_Rourke以幽默的方式指出，牛顿解释了为什么大多数人不会飘走，但没有解释像约瑟夫 of Cupertino这样的特例，此人以 alleged levitation 闻名。

• jrowen则分享了一个个人巧合，指出《Principia》出版距今338年，而自己正好在牛顿出版该书300年后出生，以此表达对牛顿及其工作的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及牛顿在《Principia》中的科学贡献，包括他对引力、电作用和神经系统中振动传导的描述。
• 出版资金问题和历史背景的讨论揭示了科学出版物在当时的经济挑战。
• 对牛顿贡献的评价存在细微差别，部分评论者认为牛顿提供了精确的数学描述，而其他人则认为这种描述并没有从根本上改变对物理现象的理解。
• 讨论中包含幽默元素，如Simon_O_Rourke对特例的提及以及jrowen的个人巧合分享。

44477768.article_content:
The Day the Universe Got Organised (Mostly)
People were worried, mostly about everything, but particularly about why things stayed on the ground. Apples fell. Horses galloped. Cannonballs soared (briefly) and came crashing down. But no one was quite sure why the moon didn’t join in and plummet to Earth in the same enthusiastic fashion.
And then on
July 5, 1687
, Isaac Newton published a book with a title so long it felt like a Latin riddle:
Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica.
In three volumes, Newton calmly explained how the universe kept its house in order. Why apples fall, why planets don’t wander off, and why we aren’t all quietly drifting into space every time we sneeze.
It Almost Didn’t Happen
The Principia might never have seen the light of day if not for Edmund Halley—the comet chap—who personally bankrolled the printing. Newton, brilliant as he was, had managed to fall out with the only other mathematician capable of understanding him. (This was the 17th-century version of crowdfunding, only with fewer emails and more quills.)
Halley’s intervention saved science from being reduced to “things fall down because they do” for another century.
How We’ve Used It Ever Since
In the 337 years since, Newton’s ideas have been used for all sorts of fussy yet vital activities: building bridges that don’t collapse, plotting planetary orbits, and explaining why toast inevitably lands butter-side down.
NASA still uses Newton’s framework today. They strap adventurous humans into enormous cylinders, set off controlled explosions underneath, and fling them into space—because three centuries later, it’s still the best idea we’ve got.
Why It Matters (Even if You Don’t Think It Does)
We treat the Principia as a sacred text, but it’s really just a rulebook for how objects behave. Big ones, like moons and planets. And small ones, like apples, cannonballs, and the pen you dropped under the fridge last week.
Newton’s laws gave us a universe that made sense—mostly. They made possible everything from satellite launches to the quiet reassurance that, barring catastrophe, your kettle isn’t going anywhere.
337 Years of Falling Down Correctly
Today, we celebrate 337 years of objects falling over in a way we can more or less predict. Physics students may still curse Newton’s name during exams, but the rest of us can be quietly grateful he wrote down the fine print of reality so we didn’t have to.
Fancy more tales of science, silliness, and improbable feats of human ingenuity?
Tune into
The Multiverse Employee Handbook
—the only podcast that treats Newtonian physics like a bureaucratic policy memo with optional tea breaks.
🎧 Listen here
and let us help you understand why the universe isn’t floating off into a filing cabinet marked “To Be Sorted Later.”

data.title: Show HN: a community for collaborating on sideprojects
data.author: 0dKD
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个项目网站的反馈及功能讨论

不同观点：
• **latexr的观点**：对项目充满热情，但认为网站当前状态缺乏有用的信息。用户不愿意仅仅为了查看少量内容而注册，并表示通常会直接关闭这样的网站且不再访问。不过，由于对项目感兴趣，可能会在未来再次查看。

• **jotaen的观点**：对网站的用户体验提出质疑。点击主页上的项目后，总是被引导到一个名为“Anonymous Lurker”的个人页面，且内容为第一人称，这让人困惑，不清楚操作的目的和预期结果。

• **westoncb的观点**：认为项目概念很有趣，可能会注册。特别提到通过非正式的副项目来促进合作的想法很聪明。不过，也同意其他人的看法，认为在注册前应该能够浏览项目和个人资料。

• **Brajeshwar的观点**：提到ODF的Solo Founders Programs运行良好，提供了一个相关链接（https://www.sfp.club），作为可能的相关参考。

• **dvh的观点**：对项目与/r/INAT之间的区别提出疑问，希望了解该项目与Reddit上的INAT社区有何不同。

• **Tanishmittal的观点**：简单表达了对项目的赞赏，没有提出具体建议或批评。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在网站的用户体验上，尤其是需要注册才能查看基本信息的设计让部分用户感到不满。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是用户对项目概念的兴趣，但这种兴趣需要通过更好的网站设计和信息展示来转化为实际参与。

data.title: Game publishers respond to Stop Killing Games claim it curtails developer choice
data.author: riffraff
data.article_summary: "Stop Killing Games"运动在欧盟达到重要里程碑，成为欧洲公民倡议，但游戏行业组织Video Games Europe表示反对。该组织认为，停止在线服务是多方面考虑的结果，当游戏不再具有商业可行性时，公司有权选择关闭服务。私服并非可行替代方案，因其缺乏玩家数据保护和内容审核，且许多游戏设计为仅在线运行，关闭服务可降低开发成本。然而，"Stop Killing Games"主张玩家购买的游戏不应因停服而无法游玩，认为这是计划报废行为，且其合法性在多国未经检验。该运动在欧盟已获超过百万签名支持，但即便成功，政策变化仅适用于欧盟地区。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在线游戏服务的持续性及相关政策对游戏行业的影响

不同观点：
• [gryn] 认为许多游戏从一开始就是设计为仅在线模式，但玩家不喜欢这种模式，因为这使得开发者对游戏有更多控制。他还提到“欧洲电子游戏”组织正在试图游说或影响立法者，以扭曲这一倡议。

• [hmry] 提出私人服务器并不是一个可行的替代选项，因为它们无法提供保护玩家数据的措施，也无法移除非法内容或打击不安全的社区内容，这会导致权利持有人承担责任。他还质疑，在游戏生命周期结束后，权利持有人如何对社区托管服务器上的非法内容负责。他认为社区服务器不必遵循出版商对内容安全性的标准是一件好事。

• [aspaviento] 质疑这项政策是否仅影响欧盟游戏，并指出欧盟的其他政策对苹果、微软、谷歌等公司同样适用。任何想在欧盟销售或提供服务的公司都需要遵守其政策。

• [tareqak] 将这一运动比作软件许可的发展历程，从专有许可到BSD/MIT再到GPL和AGPL，暗示这可能是游戏行业许可模式的演变。

• [anothernewdude] 嘲讽了“开发者选择”这一论点，认为这是弱势的辩护。他将这种辩护与反对停止燃烧煤炭的工厂主相比，认为运动背后的目的正是为了限制这些选择。

补充讨论：
• 政策对不同地区和公司的广泛影响
• 私人服务器的合法性和安全性问题
• 对开发者控制的讨论以及玩家自主选择的权利

争议焦点：
• 游戏是否应强制在线模式及玩家对这种模式的反感
• 私人服务器的可行性及权利持有人的责任问题
• 政策的地域适用性和对行业的广泛影响
• 开发者选择与玩家自主权之间的平衡

44478083.article_content:
(Image credit: Westend61 via Getty)
This weekend, the Stop Killing Games movement
reached a critical milestone
to become a European Citizens' Initiative, but not everyone is on board. Video Games Europe, a trade association representing game developers and publishers in the EU,
released a statement
on Friday pushing back against Stop Killing Games.
Video Games Europe said in its statement, "We appreciate the passion of our community; however, the decision to discontinue online services is multi-faceted, never taken lightly
and must be an option for companies when an online experience is no longer commercially viable. We understand that it can be disappointing for players but, when it does happen, the industry ensures that players are given fair notice of the prospective changes in compliance with local consumer protection laws."
"Private servers are not always a viable alternative option for players as the protections we put in place to secure players’ data, remove illegal content, and combat unsafe community content would not exist and would leave rights holders liable. In addition, many titles are designed from the ground-up to be online-only; in effect, these proposals would curtail developer choice by making these video games prohibitively expensive to create."
Related articles
The 'Stop Killing Games' initiative is close to its final deadline, and after that, its leader is understandably done: 'Either the frog hops out of the pot, or it's dead'
Stop Killing Games surges past its goals, but a possible signature spoofing campaign could cause trouble: 'This is not a Change.org petition. This is a government process'
Ubisoft's defense against The Crew lawsuit doubles down on a point we've heard many times before: You don't actually own your games
"We welcome the opportunity to discuss our position with policy makers and those who have led the European Citizens Initiative in the coming months."
Video Games Europe's case is that it can be too expensive for developers and publishers to offer private servers or single-player modes in games that lose online multiplayer support, and that open or fan-supported versions of these games could present legal liabilities for companies, particularly when it comes to cybersecurity and content moderation.
The other side of that coin, as the Stop Killing Games movement points out, is that players are paying for these games. They don't (usually) get their money back if the game is shut down, so they're effectively paying for a product that's taken away from them. Of course, developers and publishers will argue players aren't buying a product but a
license
to access a game, but that's not how many players look at it.
As the
official Stop Killing Games website
explains, "Stop Killing Games' is a consumer movement started to challenge the legality of publishers destroying video games they have sold to customers. An increasing number of video games are sold effectively as goods - with no stated expiration date⁠—but designed to be completely unplayable as soon as support from the publisher ends.
The biggest gaming news, reviews and hardware deals
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
"This practice is a form of planned obsolescence and is not only detrimental to customers, but makes preservation effectively impossible. Furthermore, the legality of this practice is largely untested in many countries."
Regardless of what Video Games Europe has to say on the movement, it's clearly gaining popularity with gamers after garnering over a million signatures for its EU petition. Unfortunately, even if the Stop Killing Games movement eventually succeeds in creating some sort of policy changes, they will only apply in the EU (and potentially the UK, as well), so publishers and developers may still be able to permanently shut down games in other parts of the world.

data.title: Laser-wielding device is like an anti-aircraft system for mosquitoes
data.author: simonebrunozzi
data.article_summary: 《Photon Matrix》是一款正在Indiegogo上众筹的激光灭蚊设备，号称能在3毫秒内通过LiDAR模块检测并杀死蚊子。设备适用于室内外，具备IP68级防水功能，可防止短时间浸水。基本版扫描范围为9.8英尺，专业版则为19.7英尺，每秒可消灭多达30只蚊子。设备还使用毫米波雷达检测人或宠物，避免误伤。电源可通过墙插或充电宝供给，充电一次可使用8至16小时。尽管该技术源于2007年，但之前的原型因安全问题未商业化。该设备设计符合安全认证要求，但具体标准不明。众筹价格分别为468美元（基本版）和629美元（专业版）。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• psadri认为需要一个能通过视频分析定位并标记飞行昆虫的iOS应用，方便用户处理昆虫。
• perihelions担心该类软件或设备涉及的安全问题，尤其是如果涉及激光等可能伤害眼睛的技术。他提到了联邦法律对商用激光设备有明确规定，并质疑设备制造商是否遵循这些规定。
• JumpCrisscross同意perihelions的观点，认为需要独立的第三方测试来验证设备对眼睛的安全性，尤其是在家庭环境中使用。
• ur-whale对该应用表示期待，但感到失望的是它无法处理家蝇等其他昆虫，认为这是一个不足。
• CyberThijs没有直接讨论功能或安全问题，而是将此产品与多年前的一个搞笑广告相比较，暗示这种技术听起来像是一个玩笑或噱头。
• jeswin提出，即使该技术对人眼无害，但可能会对无反相机传感器造成损害，引发其他技术设备的潜在问题。
• pnut指出，这种利用激光灭蚊的想法已经存在几十年了，并不是全新的概念，并提供了一个关于微软前员工用激光对抗疟疾的例子。
• emsign提出一个更宏大的应用场景，认为该技术可以扩展用于防御神风无人机等军事用途，暗示未来会有更广泛的需求。
• palata对这种技术持讽刺态度，认为这是另一种杀死昆虫的方式，表达了对这种技术存在的反感。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点主要集中在安全性和技术可行性上，特别是激光对眼睛的安全问题。

Laser-wielding device is like an anti-aircraft system for mosquitoes

Ben Coxworth

Laser-wielding device is like an anti-aircraft system for mosquitoes
The mosquito-zapping Photon Matrix is presently on Indiegogo, and comes with two types of mounts

The mosquito-zapping Photon Matrix is presently on Indiegogo, and comes with two types of mounts
While we may still not have flying cars, robot butlers or food replicators actually in our possession, you
can
now order something else you may have long dreamt of. It's called the Photon Matrix, and it uses lasers to track and kill airborne mosquitoes.
Currently the subject of an Indiegogo campaign, the Chinese-designed device is claimed to be capable of detecting a mosquito and gauging its distance, orientation and body size within just 3 milliseconds.
It does so using a
LiDAR
(light detection and ranging) module which determines the locations of objects by emitting laser light pulses, then measuring how long it takes that laser light to be reflected back by whatever it hits. When a mosquito is detected in this fashion, a second
galvanometer
-directed laser is instantaneously used to fatally zap the insect.
It should be noted that mosquitoes won't be detected if they're flying any faster than 1 meter (3.3 ft) per second. For this reason, the device isn't ideal for use on speedier pest insects such as houseflies.
The Photon Matrix can be used inside or outdoors, and is IP68 waterproof (meaning it can withstand being submerged to 1.5 m / 4.9 ft for 30 minutes)
The Basic Edition model of the Photon Matrix has a 90-degree, 3-meter (9.8-ft) scanning/killing range, which is boosted to 6 meters (19.7 ft) in the Pro Version. Both models are claimed to be capable of dispatching up to 30 mosquitoes per second. And yes, they even work in pitch-black bedrooms.
Importantly, the device additionally uses millimeter-wave radar to scan its field of view for larger objects such as people and pets. If any of these are detected, its mosquito-zapping laser will not fire.
Power is supplied via a wall outlet, or by an optional rechargeable power bank. One charge of the latter should be good for either eight or 16 hours of use, depending on which of two models is selected.
Mind you, this is not the first time this idea has been promoted. The concept of a laser-based mosquito defence system took off back in 2007, when astrophysicist Lowell Wood (one of the architects of the USA's famous Reagan-era "Star Wars" missile defence initiative) raised the idea of a
smaller, mosquito-targeting laser system
at a Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation brainstorming session on eliminating malaria.
Over the following years, prototypes were built, using freely available parts from cell phones and laser printers. A device was
patented and demonstrated by a company called Intellectual Ventures
, which was more interested in owning the patent than making a product. By 2017, despite a
demo at TED
, the prototype was still not safe for human eyes.
Perhaps optical tracking, LiDAR and laser targeting systems have evolved considerably since then. The team promoting the Photon Matrix product claims it incorporates "mandatory safety certification requirements into its design," but it's unclear exactly what standards it might meet, or whether they're Chinese or international standards.
And when we say "the team," we mean one Jim Wong, from Changzhou. There isn't a company name attached at this stage. This is also Mr. Wong's first and only Indiegogo project on record, so a
healthy dose of skepticism
is warranted before you slap a pledge down.
But assuming the Photon Matrix does reach production, a
pledge of US$468
will get you a Basic Edition, with $629 required for the Pro Version. The planned retail prices are $697 and $897, respectively. You can see the technology, allegedly in action, in the video below.
Potential backers should note that the device is presently still in functional prototype form. If you're looking for something that's already in production, you might want to check out the $339
Bzigo Iris
. Although it doesn't kill mosquitoes, it does use a laser-tracking system to highlight them for easier swatting.

文章主要介绍了Bytebot的设计理念，强调通过给予LLM（大型语言模型）访问键盘、鼠标和屏幕的权限来实现代理控制，而不是依赖复杂的API集成。这种方法模拟人类远程工作者的操作，能够适应绝大多数数字工作流程，无需定制集成，具有更强的通用性、稳健性和未来适应性。

文章指出，早期尝试通过浏览器自动化和RPA（机器人流程自动化）方式遇到诸多障碍，例如不支持拖放功能、处理2FA认证等。作者引用Rich Sutton的“惨痛教训”，强调简单方法结合计算规模往往带来最大收益。因此，Bytebot选择模拟人类与计算机的交互，而非试图为每个特殊情况构建复杂逻辑。

该方法特别适用于跨应用程序的繁琐工作流程，如在不同SaaS工具间复制粘贴、处理遗留桌面软件等，这些工作流程难以自动化且缺乏API支持。通过这种方式，Bytebot为模型提供了一种无需系统更改即可操作现有系统的能力，填补了传统代理架构无法覆盖的空白。
